_README: Coordinates are approximate institution centroids, hand-entered. THE ranks are 2026 edition where I could verify them; 'unverified' means I could not, and the SVS annexure governs anyway — never trust a rank here for an eligibility decision.

Finland.post_study: Residence permit for job-seeking after graduation; doctoral researchers are employees throughout
Finland.outlook: Stable. EU member, strong research funding, active ERC presence in your exact field.
Finland.note: The four Digital Geography Lab grants make this the densest cluster for your work anywhere.

Norway.post_study: Doctoral positions are full employment contracts with pension and sick leave
Norway.outlook: Stable and well funded. Not in the EU but in the EEA, and associated to Horizon Europe.
Norway.note: Salaries are high relative to cost of living. Tromsø is Arctic — factor the darkness honestly.

Sweden.post_study: Doctoral employment; permit rules for post-completion work have tightened in recent years
Sweden.outlook: Stable. SLU is a world centre for forest and wildlife science.
Sweden.note: Verify current post-doctoral residence rules — Sweden has changed these more than its neighbours.

Netherlands.post_study: Orientation year (zoekjaar) for graduates and researchers
Netherlands.outlook: Stable, though there is ongoing political pressure to reduce international student numbers.
Netherlands.note: Wageningen is the strongest nature-and-food-systems institution in Europe.

Italy.post_study: Doctoral scholarships (borse di dottorato); ERC-funded posts are contracts
Italy.outlook: ERC funding is strong; national funding is thinner. Follow the grant, not the institution.
Italy.note: Two large Synergy grants relevant to you are hosted here.

United Kingdom.post_study: Graduate Route: 18 months if applying from 1 Jan 2027; 3 years for doctoral graduates
United Kingdom.quota: UKRI caps international students at ~30% of each doctoral training programme, and funds fees at the Home rate only.
United Kingdom.outlook: Under real strain. THE reports UK universities in the global top 500 fell below 50 for the first time, with twelve at their lowest-ever positions amid a sector funding crisis.
United Kingdom.note: ERC-funded posts hosted in the UK are hired by the PI and sit outside the UKRI cap. That is the way in.

United States.post_study: OPT, then the H-1B lottery — which is a lottery, not a process you can plan around
United States.quota: None formally, but doctoral admission is departmental and highly competitive.
United States.outlook: Funding for doctoral students is usually good once admitted. Immigration policy has been volatile and should be treated as a live risk.
United States.note: December deadlines. Verify current visa conditions close to any application — this changes faster than any other item on this map.

Germany.post_study: 18 months to seek work after graduation
Germany.outlook: Stable. Many doctoral posts are TV-L E13 public-sector contracts.
Germany.note: Max Planck IMPRS programmes are fully funded and internationally open.

Australia.post_study: Post-study work rights, historically around 2 years
Australia.quota: RTP stipends are awarded internally by universities.
Australia.outlook: Stable, but international student policy has been tightening.
Australia.note: UQ ranks far higher in QS than THE, so it is probably outside SVS eligibility. Funding would come via the university instead.

France.outlook: Stable. CNRS hosts substantial ERC activity.

Switzerland.post_study: Doctoral positions are employment; permits tied to the contract
Switzerland.quota: None, but places are few and competitive.
Switzerland.outlook: Very well funded. Association status with Horizon Europe has fluctuated — check current position.
Switzerland.note: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships require a supervisor's acceptance first.

institutions.name: University of Helsinki
institutions.dept: Geosciences & Geography · Digital Geography Lab · HELSUS
institutions.why: Three roster names, four live ERC grants, and your proposed RESDOC supervisor. The densest single point on this map for your work.

institutions.name: University of Turku
institutions.why: NATURETIME began June 2026. A team being assembled right now.

institutions.name: UiT The Arctic University of Norway
institutions.why: ZOONOSIS starts September 2026 — the only grant in the ERC record combining wildlife trade, spillover and multispecies relations.

institutions.name: University of Padua
institutions.why: INVANISH starts October 2026. Anthropologists, ecologists and citizen scientists on species redistribution. Her prior work is on human-animal relations in India.

institutions.name: University of Bologna
institutions.why: PLANETARY EEL, EUR 11.1M Synergy to 2032. Strongest more-than-human match in the record, but methodologically distant from your computational work.

institutions.name: King's College London
institutions.why: AdaptAIR, EUR 10.0M Synergy to 2032, on climate adaptation in Ladakh. ERC-funded posts sit outside the UKRI 30% cap.

institutions.name: University College London
institutions.why: One of very few people working on both biodiversity monitoring and zoonotic risk — the One Health co-supervision your Objective 2 declares it needs.

institutions.name: University of Cambridge
institutions.why: BLOCKED on language: requires IELTS 7.5 overall with 7.0 per element. You hold 7.0 / 6.5.

institutions.name: University of Oxford
institutions.dept: School of Geography and the Environment
institutions.why: Standard-tier courses require 7.0 overall / 6.5 each, which your bands clear exactly. Higher-tier courses do not. Check the tier per course page.

institutions.name: Imperial College London
institutions.why: ADAPTA, EUR 3.0M ERC Consolidator to 2031, on tropical forest adaptation.

institutions.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology
institutions.dept: EECS / CSAIL · Urban Studies & Planning / Senseable City Lab
institutions.why: Your B.Tech is a genuine asset here. But Beery's work is image-focused rather than social, so the thematic fit is weaker than the ranking suggests.

institutions.name: Yale University
institutions.dept: Ecology & Evolutionary Biology · Center for Biodiversity and Global Change
institutions.why: Map of Life is infrastructure your Objective 1 would use. His work on gaps in digital biodiversity coverage is your detection-effort problem restated.

institutions.name: Cornell University
institutions.why: eBird is the largest citizen-science conservation dataset in existence and the clearest real-world case of the detection-effort problem.

institutions.name: University of Michigan
institutions.why: Van Berkel publishes on geotagged social media for cultural ecosystem services. Carter works on tigers and coexistence — your WII and Ranthambhore work is legible to him without translation.

institutions.name: University of Queensland
institutions.why: Extinction of experience connects to your Objective 4. But UQ ranks far better in QS than THE, so SVS probably will not cover it.

institutions.name: Wageningen University
institutions.why: Strongest nature-and-food-systems institution in Europe. Salaried doctorates, no quota.

institutions.name: Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU)
institutions.why: Your WIFORCE application. Salaried, no tuition, no nationality quota.

institutions.name: ETH Zurich
institutions.why: Salaried doctoral positions, very well funded. Requirements vary by department.
